first_impression.reaction: We Googled this because James's mum's side is Turkish and Türkiye is on our shortlist. The intro won us over by admitting most guides 'repeat folklore as fact' and saying this one marks what's sourced and what isn't. That's the honesty we never get from wedding blogs. We skimmed the traditions, then actually read the legal section properly.

journey.quote: This one follows the wedding in order and marks which details are sourced and which are simply often told.
journey.reaction: Good, someone's finally separating fact from Pinterest folklore. Makes me trust the rest of it.

journey.quote: GoTürkiye names May, August and September as the most popular months for weddings.
journey.reaction: Useful. We're 14 months out with half our guests flying long-haul, so knowing which months fill first actually matters.

journey.quote: That is one region's example, but the lesson travels: leave room between the first visit and any engagement date.
journey.reaction: A trade-off we can actually act on, not just trivia. Nice.

journey.quote: Often told, though we found no cultural or academic source for it, is the story that the groom's cup is salted and he must drink it without complaint.
journey.reaction: Love that they say this out loud rather than selling it as gospel. I'll forward this bit to James's mum and see what she says.

journey.section: Before the wedding day (Hatay study passages)
journey.quote: A Ministry of Culture and Tourism folklore study of wedding customs in Hatay, in Türkiye's south, describes how it works there
journey.reaction: Honest, but a lot of Hatay. By the çeyiz section I was skimming. It reads a bit like a uni essay, and I wanted to know what this looks like at an actual wedding with 80 guests.

journey.quote: If you are travelling with a family bindallı, pack it flat in your cabin luggage and plan time to have it pressed on arrival.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of insider detail we want. More like this please.

journey.quote: That carrying sound is the point. For a hotel or villa arrival, check the venue's music rules first.
journey.reaction: Practical and slightly funny. Exactly the type of thing we'd never think of until the day.

journey.quote: We did not find a cultural or academic source for its details in time for this guide, so we leave the specifics to your families, who will know how they do it.
journey.reaction: I respect the honesty, but 'in time for this guide' makes it sound unfinished. The gold pinning is the bit our friends would ask about most, and this is where I hoped a planner would tell me how they actually run it at the reception.

journey.quote: We found no source on its meaning, so we will only say: when the line forms, your Australian guests should join it.
journey.reaction: Cute line, but after several 'we found no source' moments in a row the wedding day section starts to feel thin compared with the henna night.

journey.quote: At Beyoğlu, the couple must attend the application together on a weekday, between 9am and 12pm or 1pm and 4.30pm, or appoint a proxy with a specific power of attorney that includes a photo.
journey.reaction: Now we're talking. Office hours, the proxy option, 'incomplete applications are not accepted'. That's the stuff that actually keeps me up at night. As a lawyer I appreciate that it's clear this is one office's list and others may differ.

journey.quote: DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept ones issued in their country, so ask which version is accepted and whether it needs an apostille before anyone books flights.
journey.reaction: Genuinely useful and specific. This is the paragraph I'd send to my parents.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller's overall advice for Türkiye is "Exercise a high degree of caution" (Level 2), due to the threat of terrorism, with higher levels in some areas
journey.reaction: My dad will ask about safety first, so I'm glad they didn't dodge it. Dated and sourced, which helps.

journey.quote: If you would rather hand the paperwork timeline to one person, [speak with a Wedded Advisor](/wonderland-concierge), who stays with you from the first idea to the last dance.
journey.reaction: Handing the paperwork to one person is exactly what I want. But 'from the first idea to the last dance' is the same end-to-end line every planner uses. What does that actually mean? Are they on the ground in Türkiye, or is it someone in Sydney emailing a local supplier?

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Wonderland actually run a wedding in Türkiye with a henna night or takı töreni? Is there a real wedding we can look at, with venue and date?
Who is physically on the ground in Türkiye on the day: a Wedded Advisor, or a local partner? Who's accountable if something goes wrong?
Can the civil ceremony be held at the venue, or do we have to go to the marriage office and then do a separate celebration?
How would a planner actually run a takı töreni at a mixed Australian and Turkish reception without it feeling awkward for our non-Turkish friends?
How many working days in Türkiye do we realistically need before the wedding to get the marriage office paperwork done?
How do guests, especially grandparents, get from Istanbul airport to somewhere like Cappadocia or the Aegean coast?

turn_offs_found.quote: who stays with you from the first idea to the last dance.
turn_offs_found.why: Generic end-to-end promise with no detail behind it. It's the line every planner uses, and it's the only bit of the page that sounds like marketing.

would_share_with: James's mum, to check which customs the family actually keeps
My parents, for the legal and Smartraveller sections

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk dates, documents and where in Türkiye your families will gather, your Wedded Advisor is a conversation away.
cta_reaction.why: Not pushy, which I like, and 'dates, documents' is exactly what we'd want help with. But I'd want to see a real Turkish wedding they've done and what the Advisor actually does on the ground before I hand over our details. This is post one of the two or three I'd read.

top_3_changes: Link or reference a real wedding in Türkiye (venue and date) that included a henna night or other Turkish customs. That's what would move us from reading to enquiring.

Replace 'from the first idea to the last dance' with one or two concrete things the Wedded Advisor does for a Türkiye wedding (e.g. handles the marriage office booking, coordinates guest transfers, briefs the davul and zurna players on venue rules).

Thin out the Hatay detail a little and add one practical planner note on how the takı töreni or halay usually works at a mixed Australian and Turkish reception, so the wedding day section isn't mostly 'we found no source'.
